reasoning.binding_constraint: Converts nearly all of the traditional balance by 2055

cost_of_next_bracket.net_effect: Converting $1,000 more in 2027 would cost $160 in additional tax at the 16% rate

benefit_of_current_bracket.dollars: today's dollars (the schedule adds up each year's tax as paid)

summary_points.why_this_amount: Fills lower tax brackets during low-income years without pushing into expensive higher brackets
summary_points.how_much_you_save: Estimated $88,328 in lifetime tax savings (in today's dollars)
summary_points.key_tradeoff: Pay tax now at lower rates to avoid higher rates on forced withdrawals in retirement. Converting more enters higher brackets where the cost exceeds the benefit.

sensitivity_notes: Moderate growth assumption (7%) — result changes modestly with ±2% variation
Large income variation across years creates significant conversion opportunities in low-income years
Long retirement horizon amplifies the tax-free growth benefit of Roth conversions
RMDs begin at age 75 (15 years from now) — converting before then reduces forced taxable withdrawals in retirement
California income tax adds about 4.0% to conversions (2027); combined federal and state rates are used in optimization
Arizona income tax adds about 2.5% to conversions (2029 to 2055); combined federal and state rates are used in optimization

rmd_summary.explanation: Converting now reduces your future Required Minimum Distributions. Without conversion, RMDs starting at age 75 would peak at $67,060/year. With the recommended conversions, peak RMDs drop to $21,879/year, saving an estimated $23,093 in total RMD taxes over retirement.
